name: onesie-calibrate
description: Use before choosing a --threshold or --assert cut, when the user has labelled records, or when CI must guard a gate. Covers onesie calibrate, reading its report, --require and --offline. The built in starter sets come calibrated already.
compatibility: Requires the onesie binary on PATH. A key is needed for anything but --print-request and --offline.

rules.short: Map only the text a person would read, never the label.
rules.why: calibrate measures how well the question reads the text. A `--map` that passes the label field, or the whole record, lets the model read the answer and flatters every number in the report. `--label` runs on the whole record, not on the mapped state, so the label never has to be in the map. `--map` is required.
rules.bad: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '{body, is_urgent}' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id'
rules.good: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id'

rules.short: Always pass --out answers.jsonl --resume --id, so a relabel or new --cuts asks nothing.
rules.why: `--out` keeps every answer as `-o json` lines, with a fingerprint in `answers.jsonl.onesie` beside it. `--resume` needs `--id`, and asks only the records the file does not answer, so fixing a label, adding labelled records or trying other `--cuts` asks nothing again for the records already answered. Pass `--resume` on the first run too, since a missing file starts fresh. A change to the questions, the model, the provider, `-i`, `--map` or `--id` makes the resume exit 2, so delete the file and its sidecar and ask again. A plain stream run can resume the same file, given the same questions, model, `-i`, `--map` and `--id`, with `-o json` and no gate or merge.
rules.bad: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent'
rules.good: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume

rules.short: Read the interval columns and the worst misses before you pick a cut.
rules.why: For a yes or no question the report has one row per cut. A row flags a record when `value >= cut`, the same test `--threshold 0.8` and `--assert 'urgent.value >= 0.8'` apply, so the cut goes into the gate as written. `catches` is the share of labelled yes records flagged, `false alarms` the share of labelled no records flagged, and `right when flagged` the share of flagged records labelled yes. Each shows the count, the share and its 95 percent interval, and on a few records the interval is the part to read: `2/2 100% 34-100%` says little. `worst misses` lists by id the records answered furthest from their label, each with the start of its mapped text on one line. Read them: a wrong label is fixed in the data, and a real miss means the question needs rewording and another calibration. A pick or rate question reports its agreement, a row per name with `found`, the share of the records labelled with it that were picked as it, and `right when picked`, the share of the records picked as it that carry its label, a table of labelled against picked, and one row per confidence cut with the share it answers and their agreement, which is where a `--min-confidence` comes from. The cuts run from 0.05 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05, and `--cuts 0.5,0.7,0.9` names your own.
rules.good: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --cuts 0.5,0.7,0.9 --out answers.jsonl --resume

rules.short: Gate the calibration with --require, using lower() or upper() on a small sample.
rules.why: `--require` turns the report into a check. The report still prints, each requirement that did not hold is named on stderr, and the run exits 1. A requirement reads `[lower|upper](ID.MEASURE) OP NUMBER [at CUT]`. The measures are `catches`, `false_alarms`, `right_when_flagged` and `auc` for a yes or no question, `agreement` for pick and rate, and `within_one` for rate. NUMBER is a fraction, so `95` exits 2. On a few records the plain value passes on luck, since 16 of 16 reads 100 percent. `lower()` compares the low end of the 95 percent interval instead, 81 percent for 16 of 16, so `lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9` fails until there are enough labelled records to back it. `lower` takes `>=` or `>`, `upper` takes `<=` or `<`, as in `upper(urgent.false_alarms) <= 0.1 at 0.9`, and `auc` has no interval. Without `at`, the cut comes from the `-f` file's `assert` when it compares `ID.value < X` or `ID.value >= X`, and `at abstain` takes it from the file's `abstain_if`. A missing cut exits 2 before any request.
rules.bad: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume --require 'urgent.catches >= 0.95 at 0.9'
rules.good: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume --require 'lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9 at 0.9'

rules.short: In CI, commit the answers file and its .onesie sidecar, run --offline, and pin -m, plus --provider when it matters.
rules.why: `--offline`, with `--out` and `--resume`, reads every answer from the file and asks nothing, so the check needs no key, costs nothing and never rewrites the file. A record the file does not answer, a missing file or a fingerprint that does not match exits 2. In CI that means the questions or the records changed, so rerun without `--offline` and commit the new file. The fingerprint names the model and the provider, so pin a versioned model such as `-m jev-1.13.0`, since an alias such as `jev-latest` moves on release. Pin `--provider` too when `ONESIE_PROVIDER` can differ between the machine that wrote the file and CI. `--offline` is refused beside `--mock`, `--print-request` and `--prune`.
rules.bad: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume --require 'lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9 at 0.9'
rules.good: onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' -m jev-1.13.0 --provider typesafe --out answers.jsonl --resume --offline --require 'lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9 at 0.9'
